stories.summary: Bring the exported overlord policy spec up to the live parked-story policy
stories.description: docs/specs/OVERLORD_POLICY_SPEC.md predates the parked-story autonomy rulings and the full-autonomy high-risk adjudication in overlord-policy.md; the README also overstates the park-and-ping floor.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-01 on 9860e3e (scratch worktree, rough stand-ins for all five HK stories applied together) - 14076 passed / 21 skipped / 1 failed; the one failure (tests/unit/test_remote_sync.py::test_ssh_run_raises_called_process_error_for_unreachable_host) is host-only (no ssh binary in the preflight container; identical on untouched master). `ruff check .` clean, scripts/check_line_limit.py OK. Two conflicts found and designed out: (1) untracking the rendered launchd files broke 61 tests in 6 files that compare them to the generator output, so that story re-renders them with a placeholder home instead; (2) a repo-root guard that shells out to git crashed tests/unit/test_node_suites.py::test_gate_fails_hard_when_node_is_missing (nested pytest with an empty PATH), so the guard must tolerate a missing git binary. With both corrections: 0 conflicts.

TARGET IMPLEMENTER: Claude (sonnet). Prose that must describe a safety policy exactly; not a weak-tier story.

WHY
The exported spec is the repo's most shareable idea, and it is out of date. The live policy (overlord-policy.md, read by the overlord at runtime) added: the parked-story decision matrix; executable rulings `split_story`, `patch_acceptance`, `mark_done` (with their evidence and fail-closed rules), `repo_issue`, `escalate_model`, `park_for_human`; the patch_acceptance FIXTURE-START/END output contract; and post-hoc audit via the decisions log.
It also contains a contradiction you must surface, not resolve: overlord-policy.md line ~72 says `full` acts "on all tiers except park-and-ping, which is always" held, while line ~115 and the table row "`risk: high` merge hold | held in dry-run and gated; the overlord adjudicates it in full" say the overlord rules on the high-risk merge gate under `full`. README.md (line ~472 "Always parked regardless of autonomy level." and the Reliability bullet at ~605-610 "regardless of autonomy level") states the stricter reading.

WHAT TO DO
1. Add a new numbered section to OVERLORD_POLICY_SPEC.md, "Parked-story resolution", describing the decision matrix and each ruling harness-agnostically (what evidence it requires, how it fails closed), plus the post-hoc audit requirement. Do not copy pipeline-internal names that are not part of the contract (file paths, env var names) except where the spec already does.
2. In the spec's tier/autonomy text, state the behavior the code actually implements for `risk: high` under `full`: read pipeline code to confirm which reading is live (grep for the high-risk merge adjudication in pipeline/ - e.g. triage / merge-park code) and describe THAT, with an explicit sentence that an adopting harness MAY keep the stricter always-hold floor.
3. Correct README.md's two "regardless of autonomy level" sentences to match the confirmed behavior (e.g. "held for a human in dry-run and gated; in full the overlord adjudicates it and records the ruling for post-hoc audit").
4. Do NOT edit overlord-policy.md (it is the overlord's live prompt; changing it changes runtime behavior). Put one line in the PR description: "overlord-policy.md lines ~72 and ~115 disagree about risk: high under full; left unchanged, needs a maintainer decision."

ONE TEST: tests/unit/test_overlord_spec_parked_resolution.py - the spec contains a heading with "Parked-story resolution" and mentions split_story, patch_acceptance, mark_done and "post-hoc"; README.md no longer contains the exact phrase "Always parked regardless of autonomy level"; the spec still contains its existing "### 3.3 Tier 3" heading (survivor). Anchor on text, never counts.

DONE WHEN: that test passes, full suite passes, ruff clean.

TARGET IMPLEMENTER: Claude (sonnet). Four small generated config files, zero code. Routed to Claude only because four production files exceed the 2-file cap for non-Claude tiers (ingest sizing warning); the edit itself is a mechanical replacement. Preflight verified this exact change: 0 failures.

WHY
The repo is public. launchd/com.fagan.pipeline.{advance-scheduler,mlx-supervisor,usage-poller}.plist and launchd/pipeline-logs.newsyslog.conf are generator output committed beside their .template files, and they contain 22 occurrences of the maintainer's home directory. Untracking them was tried in preflight and broke 61 tests (test_launchd_templates_no_routing_env.py, test_scheduler_plist_daemon_cutover.py, test_newsyslog_conf_template.py, test_acceptance_launchd_plist_portability.py, test_oa2_template_auto_triage.py, test_backend_local_provider_dispatch.py) that read them. The running pipeline reads only ~/Library/LaunchAgents/, never these repo copies, so changing them has no runtime effect.

WHAT TO DO - in exactly those four files, replace every occurrence of the literal string `/Users/jessecarroll` with `/Users/example`. Nothing else changes: same keys, values, order, whitespace. A bash one-liner is fine: `sed -i '' 's#/Users/jessecarroll#/Users/example#g' <the four files>` on macOS (`sed -i` without `''` on Linux), then `git diff --stat` must show only those four files.

DO NOT CHANGE (survivor list): every launchd/*.template file; launchd/com.fagan.ollama-num-parallel.plist (has no personal path); scripts/generate_launchd_plists.sh; any test file - in particular tests/unit/test_acceptance_launchd_plist_portability.py keeps its `"/Users/jessecarroll" not in ...` assertions (they guard the templates).

ONE TEST: tests/unit/test_launchd_rendered_files_have_no_personal_home.py - for each of the four files, assert "/Users/example" appears and that the file passes `plistlib.loads` (the three .plist files) - build the home string to reject as `"/Users/" + "jessecarroll"` so this test file itself does not contain the literal; assert it is absent from all four.

DONE WHEN: that test passes, the full suite passes (the six test files named above are the regression check), ruff clean.

[no-new-tests] - write only the single small test named below.

WHAT TO DO
In every file listed in this story's `files`, replace the literal `/Users/jessecarroll` with `~` on every line EXCEPT lines containing `"repo_root"` (plan JSON needs a real absolute path to re-ingest). stories.summary: Make the test suite clean on a fresh clone: repo personas, and no files left in the repo root
stories.description: A fresh-clone pytest fails 35 tests because personas resolve from ~/.claude/agents unless AGENTS_DIR is set (only CI sets it), and three tests leak .agent_done into the repo root because a shared spy does not stub write_done_marker.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-01 on 9860e3e (scratch worktree, rough stand-ins for all five HK stories applied together) - 14076 passed / 21 skipped / 1 failed; the one failure (tests/unit/test_remote_sync.py::test_ssh_run_raises_called_process_error_for_unreachable_host) is host-only (no ssh binary in the preflight container; identical on untouched master). `ruff check .` clean, scripts/check_line_limit.py OK. Two conflicts found and designed out: (1) untracking the rendered launchd files broke 61 tests in 6 files that compare them to the generator output, so that story re-renders them with a placeholder home instead; (2) a repo-root guard that shells out to git crashed tests/unit/test_node_suites.py::test_gate_fails_hard_when_node_is_missing (nested pytest with an empty PATH), so the guard must tolerate a missing git binary. With both corrections: 0 conflicts.

TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-weight. Pin: backend "ollama", model "glm-5.3-flash:cloud". Test-infrastructure only: `files` is empty, so NO production file may change. Two existing test-support files are edited under the authorization below; one new test file is added.

ROOT CAUSES (diagnosed in preflight, reproduced on master 9860e3e)
1. pipeline/paths.py: `AGENTS_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("AGENTS_DIR", "~/.claude/agents")).expanduser()`. CI sets AGENTS_DIR to the repo's agents/ in .github/workflows/ci.yml; a contributor's `pytest -q` does not, so ~35 tests (test_review_story_context.py, test_review_prompt_file_inventory.py, test_pipeline_review_prompt_addition.py, test_pipeline_review_max_tokens_retired.py, test_ld90_review_prompt_doc_criterion.py, test_decompose_error_detail.py) fail with FileNotFoundError "No persona named code-reviewer".
2. tests/unit/_local_agent_oracle_test_helpers.py::_finish_if_green_spy stubs oracle_result, _full_suite_result, auto_commit and worktree_dirty but not write_done_marker, so scripts/local_agent_oracle.py::finish_if_green writes `.agent_done` into CWD (the repo root, bound at import as Path.cwd() in pipeline/local_agent_common.py). Leaking tests: test_local_agent_oracle_streaming_and_calibration.py::test_finish_if_green_cold_start_terminates_on_oracle_green_only, ::test_finish_if_green_rework_round_terminates_when_full_suite_green, and test_local_agent_oracle_persistence_and_finish.py::test_finish_if_green_suite_rejections_reset_on_green.

AUTHORIZED EDITS (existing test-support files; put this justification in the commit message: "test-support only: default AGENTS_DIR to the repo personas as CI does, stub the done-marker writer the spy forgot, and fail a run that litters the repo root"):
EDIT 1 - tests/unit/_local_agent_oracle_test_helpers.py. OLD (exactly once):
    monkeypatch.setattr(lao, "worktree_dirty", lambda: True)
    return messages, commits, full_calls
NEW:
    monkeypatch.setattr(lao, "worktree_dirty", lambda: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(lao, "write_done_marker", lambda rc: None)
    return messages, commits, full_calls
EDIT 2 - tests/conftest.py. Directly after the existing block that deletes PIPELINE_*/LOCAL_AGENT_* keys (ends with `del os.environ[_key]`), insert a `os.environ.setdefault("AGENTS_DIR", <abs path of the repo's agents/ dir computed from __file__>)` with a one-line comment saying CI sets the same value. setdefault, so an explicit AGENTS_DIR still wins.
EDIT 3 - tests/conftest.py, append at end of file: pytest_sessionstart / pytest_sessionfinish hooks that, only in the xdist controller (skip when session.config has `workerinput`), record untracked top-level repo-root entries from `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=normal` (entries starting "?? " with no "/" except a trailing one) at start, compare at finish, and if any NEW entry appeared print `ERROR: the test run created untracked files in the repo root: [...]` and set session.exitstatus = 1. The git call MUST be wrapped in `try/except OSError: return set()` - tests/unit/test_node_suites.py::test_gate_fails_hard_when_node_is_missing runs a nested pytest with PATH set to an empty dir, and an unguarded git call crashes that nested session (verified in preflight).

DO NOT CHANGE: pipeline/paths.py (runtime lookup stays ~/.claude/agents), any production file, any test assertion.

NEW TEST: tests/unit/test_fresh_clone_test_hygiene.py:
- os.environ["AGENTS_DIR"] (set by the conftest) resolves to <repo>/agents and that dir contains code-reviewer.md;
- the spy no longer leaks: call _finish_if_green_spy(monkeypatch, oracle_ok=True, full_ok=True), set lao.CWD to tmp_path via monkeypatch, call lao.finish_if_green(1, messages=messages), and assert neither tmp_path/".agent_done" nor <repo root>/".agent_done" exists;
- the root-entry helper returns an empty set when its git call raises FileNotFoundError (monkeypatch subprocess.run in the conftest module's namespace);
- the helper ignores tracked/modified files and nested untracked paths, and reports a new top-level untracked file (drive it with a fake subprocess result whose stdout is a canned `git status --porcelain` listing).
Do not spawn a nested pytest in the repo root (it would itself risk littering the root).

DONE WHEN: with AGENTS_DIR unset and HOME pointed at an empty tmp dir, `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` passes except host-only tests; `git status --porcelain` shows no new untracked root files after the run; ruff clean.
